responseText:
Here’s a concise, professional follow-up you can send. I can send/schedule it for you, but I can’t actually send or schedule messages unless you grant access to your email tool or confirm you want me to provide sending instructions. See the questions and next steps after the draft.

Subject: Follow-up on delayed shipment — [Order #XXXX]

Body:
Hello [Vendor Name],

I’m following up about our shipment for Order #XXXX, which was expected on [original delivery date] but has not arrived. Please provide an updated estimated time of arrival and explain the cause of the delay.

If you cannot meet the revised ETA, please confirm what expedited options you can offer (including any additional cost) and when we can expect the shipment to be dispatched. We need this information to adjust our schedule and notify stakeholders.

Please reply by [deadline — e.g., 24 hours from receipt] with the updated ETA and planned actions.

Thank you,
[Your name]
[Your company]
[Contact phone/email]

Notes / suggested edits
- Replace [Order #XXXX], [Vendor Name], and [original delivery date] with the actual details.
- Choose a deadline you prefer (24–48 hours is typical).
- If you want a firmer tone (requesting compensation, threat to cancel, or escalate), tell me and I’ll revise.

Before I send/schedule:
1) Confirm you want this exact text (or ask edits).
2) Provide vendor email address, their time zone (or confirm “their time” means vendor’s local time), and which Monday/date you mean (or say “next Monday”).
3) Tell me how to “ping” you when it’s sent (email, Slack, SMS, or here). If it’s a channel outside this chat, I’ll need access/permission.
4) Grant permission to send/schedule using your email account (e.g., connect your Gmail) — or I can give step-by-step instructions for you to schedule it in your email client.

What I can do now:
- Finalize the draft and save it for you.
- If you grant access to your email/calendar tools, I can schedule it for Monday at 8:00 (vendor local time) and notify you once it’s sent.
- If you prefer not to connect tools, I can give a ready-to-send draft and step-by-step scheduling instructions.

How would you like to proceed?
